prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 2 columns and 1 row of equal 9:16 panels, 2 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a colouring-book drawing: contours only, in one thin uniform black line on white, most of the panel left white. Draw only the people and the few large shapes of the place (walls, doors, windows, a bed, a car). People are simple storyboard figures: hair is one smooth outline of its shape, like a cap, empty inside, with no strands, curls or waves; a face has one short line each for the eyes, brows, nose and mouth, and no stubble, wrinkles or jaw lines; a fence is its posts and top rail, a tree its outline. No texture, mesh, bricks, leaves or fabric folds; no shading, grey or solid black: dark hair, clothes and cars are outlines left white inside. Thin black panel borders, plain white gutters. Location: EXT. CITY ARTERIAL ROAD, Dusk turning to night, deep blue and orange sky.
Image 1: the location EXT. CITY ARTERIAL ROAD, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back side, with no people
Image 2: the location EXT. CITY ARTERIAL ROAD, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front side, with the left side at its right edge, with no people
Image 3: the location EXT. CITY ARTERIAL ROAD, the left-side view, facing the left side, with the back side at its right edge, with no people
Image 4: the location EXT. CITY ARTERIAL ROAD, the right-side view, facing the right side, with the back side at its left edge, with no people
Image 5: the location EXT. CITY ARTERIAL ROAD, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back side, its bottom edge the front side behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right sides, with no people
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image, by the shape of the hairstyle, the build and the outfit in outline only; never copy the photograph's detail. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: Camera on the overpass at the front side, facing down the multi-lane road toward its vanishing point between the two rows of glass office towers. The lanes are packed with traffic, white headlights coming toward the camera and red tail-lights going away. The rows of streetlights along both sidewalks are still dark.
Panel 1: Extreme wide shot, high angle from the overpass, slow push in toward the vanishing point between the towers. Dense traffic streams along the multi-lane road between glass office towers with lit windows, under a dusk sky.
Panel 2: Wide shot, high angle, slow pan along the tree-lined sidewalk from the overpass. The streetlights flicker on one after another along both sidewalks as the sky darkens over the headlights.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering.
